newsitem.title: USA: Healthy U.S. wheat may drive prices lower - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Healthy U.S. wheat may drive prices lower - analyst.

text.p: U.S. winter wheat prices could drop below $3 per bushel at harvest this summer and to around $2.50 by 1998, an Indiana Farm Bureau analyst said.

Joe Miller, director of agriculture development at the Indiana Farm Bureau, told the American Farm Bureau's annual convention on Sunday that excellent weather in late 1996 meant the hard winter wheat crop had entered dormancy in the best condition in 10 years.

"Total (U.S.) wheat production could jump from last year's 2.183 billion bushels to 2.3 billion this year and to 2.5 billion to 2.7 billion bushels next year," he said. "We would go from a rather tight stocks situation to a very burdensome stocks situation in a two-year time period."
Miller also expects wheat production to rise in minor producing countries, which could cut U.S. export sales the next two to three years.

Assuming normal weather, Miller said U.S. winter wheat prices could slide to $2.75 to $3.00 late this summer and to $2.50 to $2.75 by 1998. At the Chicago Board of Trade Friday soft red winter wheat futures for July delivery closed at $3.42- 3/4.
He warned that recent warm weather in the Plains caused some wheat to break dormancy. This wheat could be damaged if frigid cold returns and the wheat is not covered by snow.
"If this occurs in the next week or so then wheat will likely move to the $4.50 to $5.00 level rather quickly," he said.
